page.layout: One page of text, with a running head and page number at the top. Below the running head, two centred citation lines. Then the running text in full-width paragraphs, ending with a decorative tailpiece, which is not text. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: Iul.Firmicus 11. Mathef.

p.i: Nec oportet, nec licet ut de statu Reip. nefaria curiositate dicamus, &c.

main_text.p: Non licet Dæmones adiurare per modum deprecationis, quia id ad benevolentiam pertinet, qua[?] non licet ad Dæmones uti 1.Cor.10. nesocii Dæmo-num fiamus. Licet tamen per virtutem Divini nominis eos adiurando eicere, ne noceant: non au-tem ut aliquid per eos discamus, aut conse-quamur.
D. August. lib. xi. Confess. cap. 12.

Ecce respondeo dicenti, Quid faciebat DEVS antequam faceret cœlum & terram? Respondeo, non illud quod quidam respondisse perhibetur iocu-lariter eludens quæstionis violentiam: Alta, inquit, scrutantibus, gehennas parabat. Aliud est videre, aliud ridere. Hac non respondeo. Libentius enim responderim, Nescio quod nescis; quam illud unde irridetur qui alta interrogavit, & laudatur qui falsa respondit.

page.notes: Running head "QVÆST. COTTON." and page number 178 are printed at the top. The decorative tailpiece at the bottom is an ornament, not text, and is not transcribed. "nesocii" is probably a printing error for "nec socii", left as printed. "qua" before "non licet" is uncertain; it may be "quæ" with the ligature lost. The Roman numeral in "Mathef." line appears as "11." in print and is copied as printed. "Hac" is printed without the ligature, left as printed. Italic and roman boundaries are approximate in the mixed passage.
